podcast.title: Backup Band for Cliff Richard
podcast.body: Former members of the Viper's Skiffle Group later formed the backing band for Cliff Richard, another singer who was a regular at The Two Eyes. "whose backing band was made up of former members of the Vipers Skiffle Loop."

podcast.title: First Drug Reference in British Pop Music
podcast.body: The group's full name, The Viper's Skiffle Group, was the first drug reference in British pop music, taken from the autobiography of American jazz clarinetist Mez Mezrow, who was known as a dope dealer. "Mez" became slang for marijuana, and "Viper" for dope smokers. Despite the name, none of the founding members (Whiten, Booker, Van Den Bosch) smoked dope; they just thought it sounded cool. "The name of the Viper's Skiffle Group was actually the first drug reference in British pop music."

podcast.title: Occasional Collaboration with Thomas Hicks
podcast.body: Thomas Hicks, a merchant seaman who was away at sea much of the time, occasionally joined the Viper's on stage. He was primarily a country and western fan and didn't care much for Skiffle, but played it because guitars in Britain in 1955-56 meant playing Skiffle. "Occasionally they would be joined on stage by a younger Quentin's name Thomas Hicks."

podcast.title: Playing at The Two Eyes Cafe
podcast.body: The group started performing at a cafe called The Two Eyes, building a reputation to the point that Lonnie Donegan began using their material. "They started performing at a cafe called The Two Eyes, two as in the Numeral, I as in the letter, and started to build up something of a reputation."
